headline: GST jumps 23 percent, foreign buyers return, ITC reports today

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Monday, the second of November, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, GST collections had their fastest growth in over four years. Gross collections jumped nearly 23 percent in October to about 2.31 lakh crore rupees, on festive demand and a surge in revenue from imports.

Second, foreign investors are buying again. They pulled out 34,843 crore rupees over October as a whole, but turned net buyers in the last week of the month. GIFT Nifty points to a firm start this morning.

Third, results season rolls on. Reliance posted its strongest quarter ever, the state-run fuel retailers swung to big profits, and ITC reports today, with analysts bracing for a weak number.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
On Friday, the Sensex and the Nifty closed higher, with the Nifty back above the 23,000 mark. Over the week, both benchmarks gained about half a percent, led by large-cap, IT and healthcare stocks. Moneycontrol says the market value of BSE-listed companies rose by more than 22 lakh crore rupees over the week, with Ather Energy, Piramal Pharma and Laurus Labs each up more than 20 percent.

Now to the flows. Foreign institutional investors bought shares worth 3,598 crore rupees on Friday, while domestic institutional investors sold about 817 crore rupees. The Economic Times says foreign investors have put in nearly 1.2 billion dollars over the last ten sessions, ending a ten-week selling streak, as global funds rethink their bets on the artificial intelligence trade.

The bigger picture is still sobering, though. Business Standard reports the Nifty is down about 12 percent so far this year, after ten straight years of gains, hurt by higher oil after the US-Israeli war on Iran and record foreign outflows of 31.3 billion dollars. Mint notes the Sensex touched a 52-week low last month before recovering, and options turnover hit a record.

The levels to watch. Analysts quoted by Moneycontrol and Angel One see 23,150 to 23,200 as the hurdle, close to the October swing high of 23,175. Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities says a breakout there could open the way to 23,500. On the downside, support is seen around 22,800, and then 22,650. This morning GIFT Nifty was trading near 23,291, up about 205 points, which points to a gap-up open.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
A quiet week for new issues. Moneycontrol says only one IPO opens this week, and it's on the small and medium enterprise platform. The main board will be idle, but 13 companies are set to list.

Further out, the pipeline of big names is building. Business Standard reports that Carlsberg has filed an updated draft prospectus for its Indian business, Pernod Ricard is doing preparatory work pending board approval, and Coca-Cola is exploring a listing of its Indian bottling arm.

In pharma deals, RPG Life Sciences says it plans to spend 500 crore rupees on another acquisition within the next twelve months.

And one from abroad. Mint says wealthy Indians are asking their wealth managers how to get shares of Anthropic, after the AI company filed papers for its IPO last week. Getting hold of them, it seems, is easier said than done.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to results, and Reliance leads. Reliance Industries reported a net profit jump of about 41 percent in the September quarter, on record consolidated revenue. Oil-to-chemicals drove the growth. Retail profit came under pressure from spending on digital commerce, though digital commerce sales grew 42 percent. Reliance Retail's chief executive, Jeyandran Venugopal, told the Economic Times that margins should improve from next year as those online investments pay off.

In energy, the three state-run fuel retailers, Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum, together earned 30,106 crore rupees in the September quarter. That reverses a loss of 18,150 crore rupees a year ago, despite the freeze on petrol and diesel prices since May. Indian Oil posted its highest ever standalone quarterly profit on strong refining margins. But rating agency Icra warns that if crude stays between 105 and 115 dollars, the three could face under-recoveries of over 64,000 crore rupees on petrol and diesel this financial year. Separately, the government raised export duties on diesel and jet fuel, and cut the petrol export levy to zero, for the fortnight from the thirty-first of October.

In pharma, Sun Pharma's net profit fell about 36 percent to 1,988 crore rupees, weighed down by US litigation costs and the Organon acquisition. Revenue rose about 12 percent to 16,199 crore rupees, and its share of the Indian market rose to 8.6 percent. The shares still edged up on Friday. Granules India is in focus after the US drug regulator concluded an inspection of its Hyderabad plant with 11 observations; its board meets today.

In autos, Mahindra and Mahindra's exports jumped 77 percent to 7,102 units, and its board meets on the fifth. Maruti, Tata Motors, Hyundai, Eicher and TVS are also in focus after their monthly sales.

Also out over the weekend: NTPC, Bharat Electronics, Bank of Baroda, Muthoot Finance, PB Fintech and CDSL. And Varun Beverages, where Mint says a 28.7 percent jump in volumes could not hide margin pain from high packaging costs.

Today, all eyes are on ITC. Analysts quoted by Business Standard expect revenue to fall around 5 percent and profit to drop by 15 to 28 percent, dragged down by the cigarette business. ITC shares are down 27 percent this year. Later this week, Dabur reports on the fourth and Emami on the fifth.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
To the economy, and the GST numbers in more detail. Gross collections rose 22.9 percent to about 2.31 lakh crore rupees in October, the fastest growth this financial year. Collections from domestic sales rose 16 percent, while revenue from imports jumped 42 percent to 72,246 crore rupees. After refunds, net collections rose about 26 percent to 2.03 lakh crore rupees. From April to October, gross collections are up 13.2 percent to about 14.78 lakh crore rupees. Maharashtra led the states with 35,150 crore rupees.

That fits with what Goldman Sachs is saying: the Centre looks on track to meet its fiscal deficit target this year, helped by strong corporate tax collections.

New GST rules also kicked in on the first of November. Under the new Rule 14B, small online sellers can register in a state where they have no office, by declaring the e-commerce operator's warehouse as their principal place of business. The refund process is also being reformed in phases. And the CII welcomed the GST Council's decision to remove arrest powers and raise the prosecution threshold, calling it a shift to trust-based governance.

One date for your calendar. Prime Minister Modi meets the new Niti Aayog leadership on the fifth of November, as the government begins shaping next year's Budget.

On the rupee and the RBI. The rupee closed at 95.25 to the dollar in its last reported session. The RBI's net short dollar forward position hit a record 239.2 billion dollars in September. SBI Research expects the 10-year government bond yield to ease to between 6.75 and 7 percent by March, even with a possible half-percentage-point rate hike. And RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said growth could have topped 8 percent but for global shocks.

Fuel prices moved too. Jet fuel rose by 1.37 rupees a litre to 138.50 rupees, the fourth straight monthly increase, and commercial LPG went up by 10 rupees to 2,820 rupees for a 19-kilogram cylinder. Meanwhile, India's crude imports hit a record of about 5.6 million barrels a day in October, according to the data firm Kpler.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, the AI trade is wobbling. Wall Street tumbled on Friday, with the Nasdaq posting its biggest one-day percentage fall since June, after disappointing results from Intel and Amazon deepened worries about massive AI spending. Asian shares are mixed to lower this morning. Traders now brace for the US midterm elections tomorrow, US jobs data, and Nvidia's results later this month.

On the other side, the US economy grew a faster-than-expected 3.4 percent, the most in a year. The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75 to 4 percent, and Chair Kevin Warsh said the fight against inflation remains the priority.

Oil is cooling a little. Brent crude slipped more than 1 percent to around 111.84 dollars a barrel, as talks continue on ending the Iran war. OPEC plus has agreed to hold its production targets through December.

And in China, regulators meet banks and brokers today to discuss ways to support the stock market.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Now, your money. Gold had its worst October since 2008, down about 7 percent for the month, while silver fell about 19 percent. Gold bounced 0.7 percent this morning to near 3,900 dollars an ounce.

In mutual funds, small-cap funds were the worst equity category in October, down 5.83 percent on average. Technology funds were the standout, up 6.29 percent.

A few tax points. Buying a car above 10 lakh rupees this Dhanteras? The 1 percent tax collected at source can be claimed as a credit when you file your return. The Delhi bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal deleted a penalty of 3.08 lakh rupees on a salaried taxpayer who left out 4.49 lakh rupees of bank interest, citing a genuine omission and a poorly worded notice under section 270A. And Mint reminds non-resident Indians that section 54F relief is available on long-term gains from mutual funds, if the net proceeds go into a house in India, subject to conditions.

On provident fund, the EPFO has launched WhatsApp services to check your balance and latest transactions, and will automatically settle eligible inoperative accounts with balances up to 1,000 rupees. Infosys shareholders, note that the record date for the 26-rupee interim dividend is tomorrow.

Two investor warnings. Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey says the regulator is working to delist companies with no economic activity, which are used in pump and dump schemes, and it is using AI to track them. Ten penny stocks have fallen between 34 and 73 percent in three months. And AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a possible breach of customer data stored on Salesforce.

If you bank with IDBI Bank, a strike is planned today and tomorrow, so branch services may be affected. The bank points customers to UPI, ATMs and internet banking.

That's the brief. Today, watch whether the Nifty can clear 23,200 after a gap-up start, ITC's numbers, crude around 111 dollars, and how markets position ahead of tomorrow's US midterms. Have a good Monday.
